title: The English Civil War (1642–1651)
key_facts: Series of conflicts between Royalists (Cavaliers) and Parliamentarians (Roundheads)
Struggle over the balance of power between the monarchy and Parliament
Ended with Parliament’s victory and the trial and execution of Charles I
causes: Religious tensions and disputes over church governance
Fiscal conflicts and the monarch’s attempts to rule without Parliament
Competing visions of sovereignty and rights
outcome: Commonwealth under Oliver Cromwell and temporary abolition of the monarchy
Rise of constitutional debates (e.g., Levellers) and military reforms
Set precedents for constitutional monarchy finalized in 1688–89
impacts: Shift toward parliamentary supremacy and constitutional monarchy
Religious pluralism debates and limits on royal prerogative
Military and administrative innovations influencing later states
